description: Slice about 4950 cal BP, zone K-6: oak forest steppe with meadow steppe; between 5280 and 4560 cal BP Poaceae and Liguliflorae rise at the expense of Quercus. name: Halas-fenék palaeochannel (Zám-puszta, Hortobágy)
description: Holocene zone 4 (450-125 cm). English abstract: 'The pollen profile is dominated by non-arboreal pollen, even during the Holocene ... deciduous arboreal pollen did not become dominant in any one pollen zone'; at the Holocene start colder steppe gave way to milder temperate steppe with no rise in forest pollen (paraphrased from the Hungarian text). Weak chronology: only two 14C dates (>35 ka at 9 m; 5200±200 14C BP at 125-150 cm), so this slice is placed by zonation only. Pine pollen is partly flood-borne (full text).

description: Conference abstract only (Diaconu et al. 2018, EGU2018-680): 'Between 7000-6000 cal yr BP, the pollen based vegetation reconstruction show a mixed forest-steppe environment', with grass-dominated charcoal and fire every 70 years. The published paper (Feurdean et al. 2021) presents the record from about 6000 cal BP only, so this slice is weaker.

Maximum tree cover of about 50% comes later, 4200-2500 cal BP (full text, 14C cal BP).

name: Zahájí (Podbradecký potok valley, lower Ohře, N Bohemia)
description: Pollen zone Z1a (base of a ~9000-yr fen-peat record on the loess/marl lowland, about 500 mm rain at nearby Doksany; zone called Boreal by the authors, base not directly dated, slice approximate): Pinus 30-80%, Juniperus at its maximum, Artemisia and grasses dominate the herbs, frequent fires. Authors: 'a mosaic of sparse pine woods and open areas with abundant grasses, birch, juniper and hazel'. Read in the Czech companion paper (Zprávy ČBS 50); English version Holocene 25:716, doi 10.1177/0959683614566218.

name: Zahájí (Podbradecký potok valley, lower Ohře, N Bohemia)
description: Pollen zone Z1b (mid-Holocene before the Neolithic; upper boundary dated 7236-6952 cal BP at 648 cm): tree pollen 95% of the sum (the record maximum) but 40-60% of it Pinus and Betula, heavy pollen producers; Artemisia continuous, Pulsatilla, Helianthemum, Chenopodiaceae present. name: Suchý potok (near Vojnice, lower Ohře plateau, N Bohemia)
description: Land-snail sequence from a shallow treeless valley (local signal: valley floor and slopes). Lower layers dated by Discus ruderatus and 14C (8348-8192 cal BP in layers 27-28). Open-ground species dominate from base to top, steppe snails Chondrula tridens and Helicopsis striata abundant and continuous, shade-forest species almost absent; Fruticicola fruticum peak in layers 23-29 indicates 'park-like environment with islands of trees and shrubs'. Pokorný et al. 2015 (Czech companion paper read in full).

name: Suchý potok (near Vojnice, lower Ohře plateau, N Bohemia)
description: Between the dated layers (8348-8192 and 6176-5917 cal BP): 'unusually monotonous' sequence, open-ground and semi-open species (Vallonia, Fruticicola) throughout, steppe species continuous; authors take it as proof of Holocene continuity of open dry habitats in the lower Ohře region. Local (valley-scale) evidence.

name: Lake Vracov (Bzenecký potok, Lower Morava valley, S Moravia), REVEALS 25 km radius
description: REVEALS land-cover estimate for a 25 km radius (hex-scale), early Holocene 10000-6500 BC: open land ~27% (up to 30%, falling to 15% at the end), Pinus 40-60% and Betula 10-20% of trees, Corylus to ~20% late. Authors: 'open pine-birch forests'; grasslands and open woodlands 'probably maintained by local arid climatic conditions'. Chronology: Bacon model, 9830±60 BP (9446-9211 cal BC) at 280 cm, 9410±40 BP at 252 cm; early Holocene age-depth is uncertain. Implied tree cover (complement, not stated by the paper) ~70-85%, above the 20-50% forest-steppe band.

name: Lake Vracov (Bzenecký potok, Lower Morava valley, S Moravia), REVEALS 25 km radius
description: REVEALS 25 km radius, start of the middle Holocene (6500-3000 BC): open land 12.5%, 'the maximum recorded proportion of forested land'; forests mostly coniferous, Pinus dominant with Picea to ~20% and abundant Corylus. Few Holocene 14C dates (8000-1 BC is poorly constrained).

name: Lake Vracov (Bzenecký potok, Lower Morava valley, S Moravia), REVEALS 25 km radius
description: REVEALS 25 km radius, middle Holocene 6500-3000 BC: 'the ratio of open land remained high at ca. 20%'; 'forests were mostly coniferous with dominant pine and spruce', Corylus abundant. Authors: 'Neolithic people spread into a landscape that was already open'; detectable human transformation only after 2000 BC. Note the paper is internally inconsistent on whether mid-Holocene openness was lower than early Holocene. Dated level 4715±35 BP (3632-3375 cal BC) at 185 cm.

name: Svatobořice-Mistřín fen (Kyjovka floodplain, Dolnomoravský úval, S Moravia)
description: Pollen, older Atlantic (AT1; organic sedimentation begins at the start of the Atlantic on sandy-loamy alluvium; chronozone not directly dated here, slices placed by conventional chronozones): tree pollen only ~50% of the sum, which Svobodová calls an exception against ~70% elsewhere in the Pannonian lowlands; pine-hazel woods on dry sites turning into oak woods with elm and lime, alder carr around the fen. The low AP may partly reflect the local sandy setting.

name: Tišice (Labe/Elbe floodplain oxbow, central Bohemia)
description: Pollen zone T1 (ca 5500-3100 uncal 14C BP, about -4350 to -1350 cal; dates CU-1532/1543): 'regional woodlands, which still had a semi-natural character, were dominated by oak' with Ulmus, Tilia, Fraxinus, Corylus, Picea, some Fagus; pine stands on sand dunes; weak but continuous human impact. name: Ascherslebener See (former lake, northern Harz foreland), approximate basin centre
description: Preboreal cool oscillation (chronozone dating; slice approximate): sharp Pinus fall, Betula re-spreads, herbs and grasses again over 50% of pollen; Mania: 'light birch woods with pines, larger open parts of the landscape with meadow steppes'. Synthesis of pollen (Müller 1953), molluscs and ostracods from the open-cast mine sections.

name: Ascherslebener See (former lake, northern Harz foreland), approximate basin centre
description: Late Preboreal (chronozone dating): pine dominant, first thermophilous trees (Corylus, Ulmus, Quercus) appear; steppe snails (Chondrula tridens, Helicopsis striata, Pupilla sterri) present in the lake thanatocoenoses, which Mania reads as open landscape in the Harz foreland and Thuringian Basin since the early Holocene.

name: Ascherslebener See (former lake, northern Harz foreland), approximate basin centre
